title: Block A close: the long surahs
hookLine: law, story, battle and mercy woven together, and every surah but one opening with mercy

lines: LAW BESIDE PRAYER, BATTLE BESIDE HEART.
cards: Ninety-five days ago, this year began with seven verses said seventeen times a day.

Since then you've walked through the long surahs at the front of the Qur'an, most of them revealed in Medina, where a small community became a city with neighbors, treaties, marriages, markets and wars.
A reader expecting nothing but prayer finds something else. Inheritance shares sit beside the Throne verse. A debt contract sits beside a prayer for strength.
A battle sits beside a verse about a single heart. And nearly every one of those surahs opens the same way.

teach.b: Here's Block A in nine doors. Al-Fatiha: a conversation, praise and then asking.
Al-Baqarah: the cow, the Throne verse, no compulsion in religion, write your debts down, and a God who burdens no soul beyond what it can bear.
Al 'Imran: Maryam, chosen above the women of the worlds, a common word with the People of the Book, and the Prophet's gentleness: had you been harsh, they would have scattered.

An-Nisa: live with them in kindness, stand for justice even against yourselves, greet with something better. Al-Ma'idah: whoever saves one life, it is as if he saved all humanity; compete in good; the table from heaven.
Al-An'am: not a leaf falls without His knowing; don't insult the gods of others.

teach.h: NOT A LEAF; AM I NOT YOUR LORD?
teach.b: Al-A'raf: am I not your Lord, asked before we were born, and the garment of piety. Al-Anfal: if they incline to peace, incline to it too.

teach.h: PEACE; THE CAVE; ENOUGH FOR ME.
teach.b: At-Tawbah: the cave, the three left behind, and enough for me. Law, story, battle, and running through all of it, mercy. Now count the openings.
Of the Qur'an's one hundred fourteen surahs, every one opens with bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim, in the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind, except at-Tawbah.
And, as you saw a week ago, the missing bismillah turns up inside another surah, an-Naml, in a letter from Sulayman, so the phrase still appears one hundred fourteen times.
Before every law, story and battle in these pages, the reader passes through those words.
However hard the room, mercy was the door you came in by.

how: Muslims begin the recitation of every surah except at-Tawbah with bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim, and many who read the Qur'an through mark the end of the long opening surahs as a milestone in their reading.

o: God is greater, said at the start of each prayer
in the name of God: the door to every surah but one
praise be to God, the Lord of all the worlds

games.q: Block A's nine doors — tap the pairs.
p: the Throne verse; write your debts down
one life, as if all humanity

s: all nine surahs of Block A were revealed in Medina
most were; al-Fatiha, al-An'am and al-A'raf are usually counted as Meccan.
al-Anfal says to incline to peace if the other side does
8:61: if they incline to peace, incline to it too.
the long surahs keep law and prayer in separate sections
they're woven together: inheritance beside the Throne verse, battle beside the heart.

games.q: you're opening any surah of the Qur'an but one. what words do you pass through first?
o: in the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind.
games.why: bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim. every surah but at-Tawbah opens with it: mercy is the door.

practice: Let the nine doors pass by slowly, one per breath or two: the Fatiha, the Cow, the Family of 'Imran, the Women, the Table, the Cattle, the Heights, the Spoils, the Repentance.
At each one, let a single line or picture come back, whatever stayed with you. If you pray, you can begin with bismillah.

wordCard.voice: Bismillah, in the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind. The door that opens every surah but one, appearing one hundred fourteen times in all. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "in the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind," the door of 113 surahs.

carryVoice: Your line: mercy was always the door. Tomorrow Block B begins: prophets, parables and light, starting with Surah Yunus. Block A, complete.

sources.ref: Qur'an 1–9 (the long surahs of Block A)
